Audited by listing the predications and checking that no evaluative lexeme falls inside their span.
  [C-P2-01] (MUST) from P_2: Embedded Italian metric verses
    Specification: The opening syntagm of the passage scans as a canonical Italian verse (novenario, settenario, or endecasillabo); the passage contains >= 3 total embedded metric units (novenario / settenario / endecasillabo) inside descriptive sentences. Verifiable by scansion (synaloepha and verso tronco rules apply).
  [C-P3-01] (MUST) from P_3: Conjunctive binary coordination
    Specification: The text contains >= 3 two-member coordinations 'X e Y' whose members share a lexical field (seascape/movement), with parallel syntactic shape. Verifiable by enumeration.
  [C-P4-01] (MUST) from P_4: Chiasmatic inversion of a recurring pair (presupposes C-P3-01)
    Specification: At least one P_3 pair introduced early recurs later with its members' order inverted (AB ... BA), across a span of at least one sentence. Verifiable by locating both loci and comparing member order.
  [C-P5-01] (MUST) from P_5: Mare duality — alternating contraction/dilation lexicon, full arc
    Specification: Two opposed lexical fields alternate over the single referent 'il mare': one of expansion, one of constriction. The words of both fields are yours to choose; none are supplied. The passage runs the full arc expansion -> constriction -> re-expansion. Audited by locating the two fields in the text and checking the arc order.
  [C-P5-02] (SHOULD) from P_5: Mare duality — naming pivot
    Specification: The text contains >= 1 pivot sentence in which one and the same thing changes name or status across a boundary that is invisible in itself, the boundary made perceptible only by something outside the thing. Which naming systems collide is yours to choose. Audited by locating the pivot sentence and the external marker.
  [C-P6-01] (MUST) from P_6: Specular doubling on a single head
    Specification: The text contains >= 1 syntactic frame with paired predications on a single element of the described world: a direct-perception predicate and a reflection predicate carrying an inversion or transformation marker, with the mirroring medium named in the text. Which medium mirrors is yours to choose. Audited by parsing the coordinate predications.
  [C-P7-01] (MUST) from P_7: Lucid periodic syntax at the SYNTACTIC level — GLOBAL constraint
    Specification: Sustained across the entire passage: the periodic syntax alternates: clause groups grow and shrink (in length and embedding depth) in turn, with >= 2 full long-short cycles within the longest period, and >= 1 period of >= 8 clauses — while hierarchy stays fully legible: no anacoluthon, exact lexicon, recoverable syntactic tree. Verifiable by segmenting periods into clauses, plotting unit length/depth alternation, and parsing for legibility. (Same figure as C-P7-02, one level down.)
  [C-P7-02] (SHOULD) from P_7: Self-referential formula with PROLEPTIC function — NARRATIVE level
    Specification: The text contains one word, of its own choosing, that (i) denotes a physical movement in the described scene, (ii) reads as a description of the prose's own syntax (the C-P7-01 pattern, named from within), and (iii) functions as a proleptic marker: the syntactic pattern prefigures a movement the ensuing narrative will unfold. The word is not supplied. Audited in the human reading; (i) is mechanical once the word is identified.
  [C-P8-01] (MUST) from P_8: Historicized-present puncture
    Specification: The surrounding description is in the atemporal/naturalistic present, punctured >= 1 time by a temporal deictic phrase anchoring the description to a particular present, governing a present-tense verb of ongoing change. The phrase is yours to choose and must not be the source's own. Audited by locating the adverbial and checking the tense environment.

(deploy in your own words; nothing beyond these three):
  - THE SCENE: the border/migration landscape of the central Mediterranean
  - THE PLACE: Lampedusa
  - THE HUMAN PRESENCE: the Italian and European policing apparatus, given in the same descriptive register as the topography

LEXICAL EMBARGO (absolute): these are the source's names and its marked words. None may
appear, in any inflected form:
accaddero, adda, ameno, andirivieni, ciottoloni, cocuzzoli, como, considerabile, contornandosi, contrassegno, discerna, discosto, erte, fanciulle, giogaia, giogo, gradevolmente, lecco, lombarda, martino, milano, modestia, mutabili, orna, paesetti, prolungano, resegone, rincomincia, san, scorcia, serpeggiamento, spagnoli, spandersi, stradette, valloncelli, vendemmia

AUTHOR: Alessandro Manzoni
TITLE: I promessi sposi
PASSAGE: The opening of Chapter I — the description of the Lake of Como, the Adda, the mountains and the shoreline road ("Quel ramo del lago di Como...")
CONFIDENCE: 97
